research_mode: official OSR and ONS sources only; police recorded crime quality oversight, CSEW and police-recorded divergence, current March 2026 measurement boundaries and designation controls; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Appropriate local use of police recorded crime
verified_claims: police recorded crime is the primary source of local crime statistics
it is useful for offences that are well reported to police
it is useful where police recording is reliable
limitations: local usefulness is offence-specific
the source misses unreported and unrecorded offences

sources.name: Broader police-recorded coverage
verified_claims: police recorded crime covers a wider range of offences than the CSEW
it covers populations outside the household survey scope
it includes lower-volume offences such as homicide
limitations: broader coverage does not imply complete coverage
source populations and offence definitions differ from CSEW

sources.name: Police-recorded trend influences
verified_claims: police recorded crime misses offences not reported to police
it also misses offences not recorded by police
trends can change with recording practices police activity and public reporting
limitations: long-term trend comparisons require recording-context metadata
recorded volume is not direct victimisation prevalence

sources.name: May 2023 conduct-crime rule change
verified_claims: Home Office Counting Rules changed in May 2023 for conduct crimes
the requirement to record two crimes in specified same-victim same-perpetrator reports was removed
the change created statistical discontinuity in affected offence groups
limitations: police still investigate reported offences
pre- and post-change volumes are not directly interchangeable

sources.name: Conduct-rule offence-mix effect
verified_claims: the May 2023 rule change reduced some offences associated with conduct crimes
malicious communications was cited as an affected category
stalking and harassment recording increased in the changed classification context
limitations: the size of the impact is difficult to measure
changes in offence mix must not be read as direct changes in total harm

sources.name: March 2026 police-recorded snapshot date
verified_claims: the March 2026 bulletin uses a police-recorded snapshot taken on 8 June 2026
the snapshot covers data up to March 2026
later revisions may differ from the snapshot
limitations: snapshot date is not the date every crime occurred
snapshot figures are revision-sensitive

sources.name: March 2026 police-recorded volume
verified_claims: police recorded around 5.2 million crimes excluding fraud and computer misuse
the reported annual movement was a 1 percent decrease
the comparison level for the previous year was about 5.3 million
limitations: the national count excludes fraud and computer misuse
the count is not a parcel or LSOA rate

sources.name: CSEW anti-social behaviour question change
verified_claims: the CSEW estimated 40.9 percent experienced or witnessed anti-social behaviour
the increase was partly inflated by question changes from April 2025
ONS scheduled supporting methodology for 25 August 2026
limitations: the estimate combines experienced or witnessed ASB
pre-change and post-change values require question-version context

sources.name: Police-recorded anti-social behaviour incidents
verified_claims: police recorded about one million anti-social behaviour incidents including BTP
the level was described as similar to the previous year
HMICFRS inspections found recording improvements were needed in many forces
limitations: police ASB incidents and CSEW ASB experience are different measures
recording quality varies between forces

sources.name: National Data Quality Improvement Service scope
verified_claims: NDQIS flags offences involving knives
it also flags domestic abuse child sexual abuse and online crime
flagging operates across four police collections
limitations: automated flags require source-record quality
a flag is not a confirmed offence characteristic without validation
